name: Kung Fu Man (kfma4a)
notes: Transcribed by hand from C:/rw/corpus/kfm (MUGEN 1.1 / Ikemen, localcoord 320,240).
Frame counts come from the .air element durations read the way mugen_cns.py:304-330
reads them: a move connects on the first element carrying a Clsn1 box and stays
dangerous for the contiguous run of them; recovery is total - startup - active + 1
(mugen_cns.py:560-561). Hitstun is the HitDef ground.hittime.
PUSHBACK IS ESTIMATED on every move by one uniform rule -- |ground.velocity| *
ground.slidetime / 2 -- because MUGEN records a velocity and a friction, never a
displacement. It is the weakest class of number in the file.
REIKYAKU is the weakest single move: anim 1210 uses Clsn1Default, which
mugen_cns.py:304-330 says means the animation cannot say when the move becomes
dangerous, so its 4-frame startup is the HitDef's own time=0 plus the 3 prep ticks
of state 1200, and its active=2 is a fallback rather than data.
Hitstun decay is this project's house rule (linear, 2 frames per hit, floor 10), NOT
read from the CNS: MUGEN has no global hitstun decay. With KFM's 11-frame lights the
floor bites immediately, so it is very nearly no decay at all.
Character mode fixed at var(3)=1 (kfm) and var(5)=0 (the light button version of every
special): kfma4a_cns.txt:6213 sets var(3), and each special sets var(5) from which
button was pressed. The strong versions are a second, untranscribed set of moves.
Juggle is charged only on the four moves whose HitDef sets fall, because MUGEN checks
juggle only against an airborne defender (mugen_cns.py:956-958) and those are the moves
that put the defender there. Charging it on the ground chain as well would over-
constrain the model and hide the very loop this run exists to find.

engine.derivation: ESTIMATED: MUGEN has no global hitstun decay. 2 frames per hit with a 10-frame floor is this project's house rule, applied uniformly to all three Phase-0 characters so they stay comparable. NOT read from the CNS.

engine.exactness: GCD of every power value in this character -- poweradd 10/20/50/100 and getpower 20/40/50/60 and the supers' -1000 -- is 10 MUGEN power, so 1/100 bar is exact for KFM with no rounding in either direction.

engine.charged_on: only the four moves whose HitDef sets fall: f_hk_upper (statedef juggle=7), crouch_hk (9), reikyaku (8), fuyo_reikyaku (8, from state 3000). MUGEN checks juggle only against an airborne defender (mugen_cns.py:956-958); these are the moves that make the defender airborne.

engine.derivation: NOT TRANSCRIBED. KFM has no fixed-length dash: forward movement past walking is a hold-to-run (state 100, corpus/kfm/kfma4a.cmd:503-509; velocity.run.fwd=4.86, corpus/kfm/kfma4a3.txt:34), whose distance is a function of how long the stick is held. A fixed-frame gap action would be an invention, so the effect is zero and walk_speed carries the movement instead.

derivation.startup: derived: HitDef fires at time=0 (corpus/kfm/kfma4a_cns.txt:179-180) so the animation decides; anim 200 element 6 is the first Clsn1 frame and elements 1-5 are 1 tick each (corpus/kfm/kfma4a.air:695-706)
derivation.active: derived: element 6 is the only Clsn1 frame and lasts 6 ticks (corpus/kfm/kfma4a.air:707-709)
derivation.recovery: derived: mugen_cns.py:560-561 formula, total - startup - active + 1 = 21 - 6 - 6 + 1 (corpus/kfm/kfma4a.air:694-720, 21 ticks)
derivation.hitstun: derived: ground.hittime=11 (corpus/kfm/kfma4a_cns.txt:200); air.hittime is not given so min() is 11 (mugen_cns.py:568-570)
derivation.damage: derived: damage=25,0 (corpus/kfm/kfma4a_cns.txt:184); the 25 is the hit value
derivation.pushback: ESTIMATED: |ground.velocity| * ground.slidetime / 2 = 6*10/2 = 30 px (corpus/kfm/kfma4a_cns.txt:199,201). MUGEN records a velocity, never a displacement.
derivation.meter: derived: poweradd=10 (corpus/kfm/kfma4a_cns.txt:173) + getpower=20 on hit (corpus/kfm/kfma4a_cns.txt:207) = 30 MUGEN power = 3 units at 1/100 bar

events.note: voice, kfma4a_cns.txt:226-230; the original is gated on random<300, which a deterministic sim cannot use, so it always plays

reaction.guard_ctrltime: AUTHORED AS AN EXPRESSION, NOT A NUMBER: guard.ctrltime = id + 0*(var(31):=0 || var(30):=510562) (kfma4a_cns.txt:210). The character abuses the field to stash hit-spark coordinates in variables; the actual control time is the player id. Not transcribable and not transcribed.

fx.note: sparkxy=-10,-62 (kfma4a_cns.txt:186); hitsound/guardsound are ifelse(sysfvar(0)>0,...) expressions (kfma4a_cns.txt:191-192), the sysfvar(0)<=0 branch is taken

engine.transcription_note: far version: the .cmd picks 210 vs 220 on p2bodydist x<26 (kfma4a.cmd:575). A MINIMUM range is not expressible: the prover's guard says 'space >= n', which is a maximum gap, never a minimum.

escape_hatch.reason: minimum-range requirement (p2bodydist x >= 26). The guard vocabulary can only say 'space >= n', which is a maximum gap. The engine's input layer needs a runtime distance test to choose 210 vs 220.
escape_hatch.what_it_needs: move.min_reach (float, reach units): the mirror of move.reach. Note the PROVER cannot use it -- model.py:453-458 only ever writes a 'space >= n' guard -- so this closes the engine side and leaves a documented modelling gap on the prover side.

engine.transcription_note: far version: the .cmd picks 230 vs 240 on p2bodydist x<16 (kfma4a.cmd:621). Same minimum-range problem as stand_hp_far.

escape_hatch.reason: minimum-range requirement (p2bodydist x >= 16). Same as stand_hp_far.

engine.transcription_note: state 275 carries TWO HitDefs (animelem=4 and animelem=10, kfma4a_cns.txt:790,830). Only the first is transcribed, exactly as mugen_cns.py:530-535 does. The second hit (damage 30, ground.hittime 23) is dropped.

escape_hatch.reason: two HitDefs in one state. Move carries exactly one startup/active/hitstun/damage, so the second hit has no home.
escape_hatch.what_it_needs: move.engine.hits[] (list of {frame, damage, hitstun, reaction}) with the [P] fields taken from hits[0]. Prover-side, a multi-hit state stays one Move.

engine.transcription_note: holding forward swaps the animation to 450 and the move becomes a different attack with a different HitDef (kfma4a_cns.txt:1092-1100,1103). Only the neutral (anim 440) version is transcribed.
state 1010 carries TWO HitDefs (animelem=10 and animelem=16); only the first is transcribed (mugen_cns.py:530-535). startup folds in the 4 ticks of state 1000 (anim 1000, 4 elements of 1 tick).

escape_hatch.reason: two HitDefs in one state, plus a landing-conditioned exit (time>18 && pos y+vel y>=0 && vel y>0).
escape_hatch.what_it_needs: move.engine.hits[], plus move.engine.exit_condition for the landing test.

engine.transcription_note: PROJECTILE. The 15 frames are until the fireball is released (animelem=10 of anim 1100). Time-to-contact depends on distance and is NOT in startup. reach is null because a fireball has no range limit; that is the closest the schema can get.

escape_hatch.reason: projectile: the frame the attack connects is a function of distance, and Move.startup is a constant.
escape_hatch.what_it_needs: move.engine.projectile {spawn_tick, velocity_sub, lifetime_ticks, hitdef}. Prover-side, Move.startup being a constant while a fireball's contact frame is a function of distance is a limit of the fragment, not of the schema.

engine.transcription_note: WEAKEST NUMBERS IN THE FILE. anim 1210 uses Clsn1Default (blanket boxes), which mugen_cns.py:304-330 says means 'the animation cannot answer when it becomes dangerous'. startup is the 3 ticks of state 1200 plus the HitDef's own time=0, and active=2 is mugen_cns.py's fallback, not data.
three chained states (1700 -> 1710 -> 1720 -> 1730). Only state 1710's HitDef is transcribed; state 1720's second hit (damage 80) is dropped. startup folds in the 22 ticks of state 1700.

escape_hatch.reason: two HitDefs across two chained states.

engine.transcription_note: state 3010's second HitDef uses air.velocity = -vel x, vel y-1.35-pos y/686.68 (kfma4a_cns.txt:4060-4070): the launch depends on the defender's live position. Not transcribed; only the first HitDef is.

escape_hatch.reason: hit properties are a formula over live state (air.velocity = -vel x, vel y-1.35-pos y/686.68) and the first HitDef re-arms across animelems 5-8 while !movecontact.
escape_hatch.what_it_needs: nothing declarative: air.velocity = -vel x, vel y-1.35-pos y/686.68 is arithmetic over the defender's live position. This is the move that names what Phase 5's expression language has to be able to say.

engine.transcription_note: PROJECTILE, same limitation as hasyo. The 14 frames are until release (animelem=10 of anim 3200); the -1000 power is charged at animelem=5.

quantized_sources.walk_speed_note: velocity.walk.fwd = 2.4 px/tick (corpus/kfm/kfma4a3.txt:32). The engine integrates 614 sub-units/tick, which is exact. The prover's coarse view is not: walk_speed 0.024 goes through model.py:466's int(round(v*100)) and comes out 2 px/tick, losing 0.4 px/tick. The loss UNDER-states the attacker's ability to close distance, which can hide an infinite but cannot invent one.
quantized_sources.pushback_rule: round(|HitDef ground.velocity| * HitDef ground.slidetime / 2), half away from zero, applied to every move without exception. ESTIMATE.

derivation_defaults.startup: derived: the tick on which the first Clsn1 element of the animation begins (mugen_cns.py:304-330 attack_window). Every attacking state in this character declares its HitDef on frame 0, so the animation is what says when the move is dangerous.
derivation_defaults.active: derived: length of the contiguous run of Clsn1 elements
derivation_defaults.recovery: derived: mugen_cns.py:560-561 formula, total - startup - active + 1, over the animation's own tick total
derivation_defaults.hitstun: derived: HitDef ground.hittime, taken as min with air.hittime where both are given (mugen_cns.py:568-570)
derivation_defaults.reach: derived: Clsn1 x2 in px, from the same element the startup came from
derivation_defaults.pushback: ESTIMATED: round(|HitDef ground.velocity| * HitDef ground.slidetime / 2), the same rule on every move in the file, half away from zero
derivation_defaults.meter: derived: statedef poweradd + HitDef getpower (the on-hit value), divided by 10, giving units of 1/100 bar
derivation_defaults.note: A move whose engine.derivation is the string 'see engine.derivation_defaults' was read by exactly these rules with no exception. A move that carries its own object had at least one field that needed saying differently.

light_chain.condition: self.move_connected   // MUGEN movecontact: true on hit AND on block
light_chain.caveat: the same trigger also fires on WHIFF after 6 frames (time>5). Only the movecontact branch can continue a combo, so the edge is authored once, as on='always'.

special_cancel.condition: self.combo_flag   // var(41), set by movecontact on a cancellable normal
special_cancel.source: corpus/kfm/kfma4a.cmd:347-356 sets var(41) when movecontact and stateno is one of 200,210,230,260,400,410,430 (or 275 past animelem 10); :342-346 clears it the next frame; target triggers at corpus/kfm/kfma4a.cmd:416-484 (statetype!=a && (ctrl || var(41)))
special_cancel.caveat: gated on var(41), which the .cmd clears on any state change, and on !ishelper && var(51)<1 (AI level). No importer can evaluate either.

super_cancel.source: corpus/kfm/kfma4a.cmd:347-356 sets var(41) when movecontact and stateno is one of 200,210,230,260,400,410,430 (or 275 past animelem 10); :342-346 clears it the next frame; target triggers at corpus/kfm/kfma4a.cmd:363-387 (triggerall=power>=1000, trigger1=statetype!=a && (ctrl || var(41)))
super_cancel.caveat: same var(41)/var(51) gate as special_cancel. power>=1000 is carried as the TARGET move's own guard {meter:100}, not on the edge, per the schema's rule about not restating the target's cost.

command_normal_cancel.caveat: same var(41)/var(51) gate as special_cancel. The 'stateno!=275' clause is why f_lk_cancel has no self-edge.

moves_with_no_outgoing_cancel.why: This is real, not an omission. var(41) is set only from states 200, 210, 230, 260, 400, 410, 430 and 275 (kfma4a.cmd:347-356), so the far normals, the sweep, the launcher and the F+A kick are combo ENDERS by construction; specials and supers never set it either. The air normals trigger only on 'statetype=a && ctrl' (corpus/kfm/kfma4a.cmd:668-701), so a jump-in is a LINK on landing, not a cancel, and the landing frame is not in the state data -- authoring a link edge would have been an invention.

fit.gate_reading: Two numbers, both reported because the gate wording is ambiguous and the difference is the whole finding. 8 of 24 moves cannot be written in schema v1 AS IT STANDS. But 7 of those 8 need one more DECLARATIVE FIELD -- a per-move hit list, a min_reach, a projectile block -- not code. Exactly one move, fuyo_reikyaku, needs a value that is arithmetic over the defender's live position, which is the only place a C++ escape hatch or an expression language is genuinely required. Against 'needs code', the rate is 1/24 = 4% and the gate passes with room. Against 'schema v1 is complete', it is 33% and v1 needs three more fields.

verdicts_measured.midscreen: TERMINATING, general fragment, 201 configurations, 39 of 87 cancels usable, worst case 4 hits / 25 frames / 170 damage, ~890 ms in the Python reference
verdicts_measured.corner: INFINITE, 8 configurations, ~12 ms. The loop is stand_lp into itself with 4 spare frames -- KFM's own 4-way light chain (kfma4a.cmd:565-570 etc.), which is the real character's real corner infinite.
verdicts_measured.unknown_rate: 0 of 2 stages. Status::Unknown was never produced, at any decay setting tried.
verdicts_measured.sensitivity: Verdict is stable under decay = none, linear(2, floor 10) and linear(2, floor 6): midscreen terminating and corner infinite in all three.
verdicts_measured.note_on_decay: The house-rule decay is doing more work here than it did on KFG. Linear step 2 with floor 10 settles after 7 hits, and every KFM hitstun (11..23) settles to exactly 10, so the structural pass keeps only cancels into moves with startup <= 10. That is why 48 of 87 authored edges are reported dead. The verdict does not change without decay, but the dead-cancel list would.

known_losses: Random-gated controllers (voice at kfma4a_cns.txt:226-230, random<300) cannot exist in a deterministic sim; the effect is made unconditional.

getpower is folded into the meter effect here, but the paper's own importer reads only poweradd (mugen_cns.py:592-600), so our meter gains are larger than a mugen_cns import of the same character would produce.

The prover has no airborne-defender state, so the juggle resource is charged unconditionally on the four launchers rather than only when the defender is in the air. Over-constrains those moves; can hide an infinite, never invent one.
Pushback is estimated from velocity * slidetime / 2 on every move; MUGEN does not record a displacement.
givepower (the defender's meter gain) is commented out throughout this character and has no home in the prover's single-character model anyway.

Every special and hyper exists in a light and a strong version selected by var(5) from the button pressed; only the light version is transcribed. The strong versions differ in damage, poweradd and cost.

var(3) (character type, kfma4a_cns.txt:6213-6223) gates whole moves in and out: nishi (1300) and meikyo (1400) need var(3)=2 and are absent from this file, and the hy4 super resolves to 3400 rather than 3100. A mode variable that adds and removes moves is not a per-move field, so it is fixed at 1 for this transcription.

guard.ctrltime is authored as an assignment expression that stashes hit-spark coordinates in variables (kfma4a_cns.txt:210); the field's nominal value is the player id. Not transcribable, and blockstun is therefore absent from every reaction block.
The .cmd's var(51) (AI level) and !ishelper conditions gate every cancel and cannot be evaluated by any importer; all special/super edges carry certain=false because of it.
